name: Framer Motion Shared Layout Transition
description: Two phases of the same content (e.g. thumbnail → hero) share a layoutId. Framer Motion measures the start state, the end state, inverts the delta, plays the transform back to identity, and releases — the full FLIP technique handled automatically. Sub-elements (image, title, meta) carry their own layoutIds so they morph in coordinated parallel rather than crossfading. CSS keyframes cannot express this without imperative measure-and-invert code per element.

expand_at_ms.description: When to trigger the expand transition (ms from scene start).

collapse_at_ms.description: When to trigger the collapse back to the thumb state (ms from scene start).

stiffness.description: Spring stiffness on the layout transition. Higher = snappier morph.

when_to_use: Thumbnail-to-hero reveals where the same content should feel like one element morphing, not two crossfading
Card-to-modal patterns where preserving identity through the transition is the point
Editorial scenes that want a content-first morph rather than a kinetic stagger
when_to_avoid: Pure entrance animations where there's no 'start' state to measure from — use lib-framer-spring-stagger instead
Scenes with many elements morphing simultaneously — Framer's layout measurement scales linearly with layoutId count
Vanilla HTML scenes — this requires React for AnimatePresence + LayoutGroup
ai_guidance: Showcase of Framer Motion's killer feature: layoutId-driven shared element transitions. The two phases render different markup but share layoutId values, so Framer Motion correlates them and animates the geometry. Sub-elements carry their own layoutIds (cardA-image, cardA-title, cardA-meta) so they morph in coordinated parallel. No capture adapter required — Framer Motion rides on patched rAF + performance.now(). Pin React via ?deps=react@19.0.0 on every esm.sh dep — without it, motion/react imports a second copy of React and useContext fails.
